summary: Full text of the 2025 Nutr Rev meta-analysis shows theanine alone (100-400 mg, acute) improved choice reaction time in the first hour (SMD -0.35, 95% CI -0.61 to -0.10) but not most other cognitive tasks, relaxation or sleep; combination effects are attributed to caffeine. It gets one eligible context with mixed results recorded, limited to Focus & Mental Clarity. The 2014 combination meta-analysis is abstract-only and gets no credit. The new applicability block does not include the record's stress claim, which the source does not support.

applicability.studied_population: Healthy adults given acute L-theanine alone (100-400 mg) in laboratory crossover trials pooled by PMID 40314930; choice reaction time improved in the first hour, most other measures did not.

identity.preparation: Theanine-alone arms (100-400 mg) versus placebo are the credited comparison; theanine-plus-caffeine and tea-beverage arms are separate exposures and carry no theanine credit.

population.description: Healthy participants; 16 trials (15 references) in at least one meta-analysis, 484 participants (229 female), median n 27, weighted mean age 32; mostly laboratory crossover studies. Theanine-alone CR-time analysis pooled Kahathuduwa 2017, Dassanayake 2022, Haskell 2008 and Dodd 2015.

study_contexts.study_design: PROSPERO-registered (CRD42022351601) systematic review (49-50 RCTs) and random-effects SMD meta-analysis of acute cognition and mood outcomes at hour 1 and hour 2 after intake; sleep outcomes synthesized narratively.

outcomes.name: Theanine alone vs placebo, choice reaction time hour 1: SMD -0.35 (95% CI -0.61 to -0.10; P=0.02) using the 100 mg Dassanayake arm (about -18 ms); -0.32 (-0.64 to 0.01) with the 200 mg arm and -0.35 (-0.62 to -0.08) with 400 mg.

Theanine alone vs placebo, other tasks: simple reaction time, CR accuracy, CR time hour 2, digit vigilance, RVIP hour 1 and serial subtractions showed no clear difference; RVIP hour 2 favored theanine only with the 400 mg arm.
Relaxation (2 studies) CIs included no difference; sleep outcomes inconsistent (narrative).

limitations: No blanket sleep, cognition or mood claim from this heterogeneous evidence.
Do not attribute caffeine-combination benefit to theanine alone.

Results Study Characteristics explicitly reports two black-tea studies, two green-tea studies and one tea intervention in capsule form; isolated-compound arms remain separate and their delivery is not inferred. Other included trials may not report a delivery form; this list does not establish one common preparation across all arms.

Credit is limited to a small acute choice-reaction-time benefit of theanine alone in healthy adults (Focus & Mental Clarity); most other theanine-alone cognitive measures were null. The source does not support the record's stress/anxiety claim (relaxation CIs included no difference).

Few, small, mostly industry-funded laboratory crossover studies; the source states CIs often could not rule out no difference. Theanine-arm delivery forms are not tabulated; recorded as trial-specific oral preparations.

dose.administration_frequency: Mostly single acute doses with testing in the first and second hour after intake (Table 2); a few multi-week studies in the narrative review.
co_therapies: Caffeine is an active co-intervention in combination arms, which are excluded from this record's credit; tea beverages contain caffeine and polyphenols.
dose.reported_regimen: Theanine-only, low-caffeine or caffeine-free interventions: median theanine 200 mg (IQR 100.45-212.5); pooled theanine-alone arms include 100, 200 and 400 mg (Dassanayake 2022) and 100.6 mg (Baba 2021). Combination arms: median theanine 82 mg with median caffeine 88.74 mg (not credited).

normalization.basis: A heterogeneous synthesis has no single assigned-arm dose. Descriptive regimens do not create an intake recommendation, equivalent preparation or efficacy threshold.

source_provenance.location: Full text (PMC12422004): Methods (PICOS table, outcomes), Results study-selection paragraph (doses, vehicles, funding), Table 2 study summary, theanine-versus-placebo SMD table, Sleep and mood results, Discussion.

clinical_review.notes: No credit: abstract-only source whose positive findings are for caffeine plus L-theanine combinations, with moderator analysis pointing to caffeine dose; it cannot isolate theanine.

source_provenance.location: PubMed abstract (Nutr Rev 2014; full text not open access).

limitations: Camfield 2014: 11 placebo-controlled acute studies of L-theanine and EGCG alone or with caffeine; moderate effects favored combined caffeine and L-theanine for alertness and attention switching in the first 2 hours, with effect size tracking caffeine more than theanine dose (abstract). Combination evidence is not theanine-alone evidence.
